## Purpose and scope

Describe what changed, why it is necessary, and the source of requirements. Clearly identify whether the change is synthetic research, an internal prototype, a pilot candidate, or production functionality.

## Verification performed

- [ ] List exact test commands, environment, results, and supporting run URLs.
- [ ] Disclose known failing checks, unresolved reviewer threads, or untested platform-specific behavior.
- [ ] Review dependency branches, base/head SHA changes, and downstream integration requirements.
- [ ] Confirm no production deployment, FAA applicability decision, certification, or human approval is being inferred solely from CI or local tests.

## Data, intellectual property, and privacy

- [ ] No API credentials, secrets, private keys, or production configuration.
- [ ] No personal chats, personal financial/health information, residential contact details, private business correspondence, or customer/confidential records.
- [ ] No unpublished partner pricing, prospect research, contractual terms, procurement proposals, or proprietary/licensed data unless publication is explicitly authorized.
- [ ] Synthetic sample data are labeled and sources, licenses, and limitations are documented.
- [ ] Review PR description, screenshots, CI logs, attached files, and commit messages for unintended disclosure.

## AeroCIE evidence and release controls (if applicable)

- [ ] SHA-256/source pinning, original-source applicability, and stale/missing evidence paths considered.
- [ ] Relevant FAA or Federal Register metadata are represented as research only until independent human applicability review.
- [ ] Any previously reported P0/P1 or P2 defect has a fix plus regression test; unresolved threads are not represented as approved.
- [ ] Customer ingestion, external release, merge, and deployment remain separate authorized decisions.
